key_insight: PIER improves time-series environmental prediction by combining standard embedding retrieval with a physics-aware retrieval stream that checks whether candidate systems have matching flux-response behavior.
engineering_relevance: The framework is model-agnostic, so it can be added to many forecasting backbones to transfer knowledge across environmental systems while preserving physical consistency.
method: Retrieve similar scenarios using embedding similarity.
Score candidates with local physics verifiers built from flux-derived features.
Learn adaptive per-scenario weights to balance embedding and physics streams.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experiments on 356 lakes across 41 years in the Midwestern United States, showing consistent gains for water temperature and dissolved oxygen prediction.
watch_item: The physics-aware stream depends on reliable flux-derived features and trained local verifiers, which may be sensitive to feature quality and domain-specific setup.
paper_title: PIER: Physics-Informed Environmental Retrieval for Time-Series Modeling
